platform.value: Cygnus cargo vehicle (Orbital ATK CRS OA-7), free-flying after departing the ISS

sources.note: PSI-100 approach: the Saffire-III experiments were performed on the Orbital ATK Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.

NASA Saffire overview: Saffire-III launched 18 April 2017 on Orbital ATK's seventh commercial resupply mission and was ignited after the Cygnus module departed the station, before destructive reentry.

platform.note: Crew are absent; the fire burns in the uncrewed, free-flying Cygnus after it leaves the ISS. PSI lists the flight platform as ISS (the cargo vehicle's origin), not the burn location.

objective.value: Determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity and investigate low-gravity flammability limits compared with NASA's normal-gravity material flammability screening test

sources.note: PSI-100 Objectives field states the two objectives: how fast a large-scale fire grows in low gravity, and the low-g flammability limits versus normal-gravity screening.
Challenge brief, Background: flammability studies of solid materials (BASS/BASS-II/Saffire) inform prevention through material selection and flammability limits.
PSI-100: results determine microgravity flammability limits for spacecraft materials and help validate NASA's material selection criteria (prevention).

safety_functions.note: Brief groups Saffire under prevention/material selection; PSI confirms the flammability-limits and material-selection framing.

sources.note: PSI-100 approach: Saffire-III used SIBAL as the sample material (a solid fabric).
NASA Saffire overview: Saffire-III tested the same cotton-fiberglass blend (a solid cloth) burned in Saffire-I, at a higher flow velocity.

value: SIBAL cloth (composite of about 75% cotton and 25% fiberglass)

sources.note: PSI-100 approach and experimental table name the sample material as 'SIBAL fabric'.
NASA Saffire overview describes SIBAL cloth as a composite of 75% cotton and 25% fiberglass.
NASA Saffire plan (NTRS 20150000894): the Saffire I and III samples are 40.6 cm by 94.0 cm of cotton/fiberglass blend (Sibal cloth), 75% cotton by weight.

fuel_geometry.value: Thin flat sheet, 94 cm long x 40.6 cm wide x 0.33 cm thick

sources.note: PSI-100 experimental table (PSI-100_Experimental table_SAFFIRE-3.csv): samples S1 and S2 are SIBAL fabric, thickness .33 cm, length 94 cm, width 40.6 cm.
NASA Saffire plan gives the Saffire I/III sample as 40.6 cm by 94.0 cm, consistent with the PSI table dimensions.

facility.value: Cygnus cargo vehicle (uncrewed, after ISS departure)

sources.note: PSI-100 approach: experiments performed on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.
NASA Saffire overview: experiments ignited in a Cygnus cargo vehicle after it completed its ISS supply mission and before destructive reentry.

apparatus.value: Saffire III experiment enclosure in the Cygnus vehicle (flow duct and avionics bay)

sources.note: PSI-100 experimentHardware names the hardware 'Saffire III enclosure in Cygnus'.
NASA Saffire overview describes the Saffire-I enclosure as about 0.5 m wide by 1 m deep by 1.3 m long, consisting of a flow duct and avionics bay.

apparatus.note: PSI names the Saffire-III enclosure; the flow-duct plus avionics-bay description is given for the Saffire family (stated for Saffire-I), so it is not confirmed as identical for Saffire-III.

sources.note: ICES-2021-266 Table 2 lists Saffire-III sample III-1 at 21% oxygen concentration.

o2_percent.note: Only one Saffire-III condition is reported (flight sample III-1); the PSI experimental table has no oxygen column.

sources.note: ICES-2021-266 Table 2 lists Saffire-III sample III-1 at an ambient pressure of 100 kPa. Converted to psi for this field (100 kPa = 14.5 psi).

pressure_psi.note: Converted from 100 kPa to 14.5 psi; the source reports pressure in kPa, not psi.

airflow.note: reset by verifier: PSI-100 approach and experimental table state 30 cm/s, but ICES-2021-266 Table 2 (peer-reviewed flight results) lists Saffire-III sample III-1 at 25 cm/s. Two credible primary sources conflict; no basis to prefer one.

sources.note: PSI-100 Project Type is 'Microgravity Investigation'; the experiment burned in the free-flying Cygnus in orbit.
NASA Saffire overview frames Saffire as studying fire behavior in microgravity aboard the orbiting Cygnus vehicle.

gravity_g.note: Microgravity approximated as 0 g (free fall in orbit).

diluents.note: reset by verifier: recorded as nitrogen with confidence inferred from 21% O2 air-like atmosphere, but no source (PSI, NASA PDF, ICES paper, NTRS plan) explicitly states the diluent for Saffire-III.

value: Flow direction relative to the sample (concurrent vs opposed)

sources.note: PSI-100 experimental table: sample S1 tested in concurrent flow and S2 in opposed flow; approach states the flow was either concurrent or opposed.

variables_swept.note: Within Saffire-III the two tests differ in flow direction; the PSI approach also contrasts Saffire-III with Saffire-I (30 vs 20 cm/s).

value: Sample dimensions (94 cm x 40.6 cm x 0.33 cm)

sources.note: PSI-100 experimental table: both samples use SIBAL fabric with identical thickness, length, width and air flow (30 cm/s); only direction differs.

value: Solid-state sensors (pressure, CO2 and O2 mole fraction)

sources.note: PSI-100 approach lists thermocouples, two radiometers, solid-state pressure/CO2/O2 sensors, two anemometers, and two cameras capturing flame images.

relevance_notes.value: Named in the brief as a solid-material flammability study for fire prevention/material selection. PSI states Saffire-III measures large-scale microgravity fire growth and low-g flammability limits to validate NASA's material selection criteria, making it directly relevant to habitable-crew-environment fire safety.

sources.note: Challenge brief, Background: flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire-I, -II, -III).
PSI-100 objective and research impacts: large-scale fire growth and low-g flammability limits to validate material selection criteria for spacecraft fire safety.

value: Fire safety and prevention in confined spaces on Earth such as mines, airplanes and submarines

sources.note: PSI-100 Research Impacts/Earth Benefits: studying fire in small sealed environments like the Cygnus benefits fire safety and prevention on Earth, including inside mines, airplanes or submarines.
